items.quote: is money the ultimate measure of success? Let’s take a quick economics lesson (don’t worry, it’ll be painless). According to Karl Marx—basically the original economist influencer, except his posts were books—money serves only three simple functions: 1. A universal equivalent – simplifying trade.
items.statement: Success is not ultimately defined by money.

items.quote: money serves only three simple functions: 1. A universal equivalent – simplifying trade. 2. A means of exchange – accelerating the movement of goods in the economy. 3. A store of value – allowing wealth to accumulate.
items.statement: Money serves three functions according to Karl Marx: universal equivalent, means of exchange, and store of value.

items.quote: the real question we should be asking ourselves is this: If money disappeared tomorrow, what skills, knowledge, and competencies would you have to rebuild your wealth?
items.statement: Focus on skills, knowledge, and competencies to rebuild wealth if money disappeared.

items.quote: True success isn’t about the number in your bank account; it’s about the abilities that make you valuable in any market, under any economic condition.
items.statement: True success isn’t about the number in your bank account; it’s about abilities that make you valuable.

overview: LinkedIn post discussing the concept of success and value beyond money for real estate agents.
